summary: Suppose not. Let c(k) be the normalized maximal k-th Taylor coefficient of the powers of φ; it is submultiplicative (addition law of φ), and c(n) < 1, so c(k) → 0. Then the coefficients of the formal parameter S of `exists_formal_parameter` of degree ≥ l are in the maximal ideal, so S̄ = S mod 𝔪 is a polynomial P; but S̄ − S̄^{p^e} = X, i.e. (X − X^{p^e})∘P = P − P^{p^e} = X, is impossible for a polynomial (its degree is p^e·deg P ≠ 1).

steps.claim: Assume the contrary: |n!·f_n| < (p^{ρ_p−1/(p−1)})^n for every f ∈ 𝔬[[φ]].
Facts: p > 1; every power of φ lies in 𝔬[[φ]]; and from `exists_formal_parameter`: e ≠ 0, ϖ with |ϖ| = p^{−ρ_p}, π with |π| < 1, S with S − S^{p^e} = X + πE, and T ∈ 𝔬[[φ]] with T(ϖX) = ϖS.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨⟨⟩, m, e, ϖ, θ, S, _, ⟨he, hϖ, -, π2, -, E, _, hT, hS⟩, -⟩ :=
    Prime.one_lt' p, C.phiSeriesRing.pow_mem C.isSeriesGenerator_translatedWpDeriv.generator_mem,
    C.exists_formal_parameter

steps.claim: For every k choose j_k such that the k-th coefficient of φ^{j_k} has maximal norm among the k-th coefficients of elements of 𝔬[[φ]] (H).
steps.lean: choose j _ H using (exists_monomial_max_norm_coeff C.phiSeriesRing rfl 1 <| .single () ·)

let c n := ‖n ! * (taylorVia ιₚ C.translatedWpDeriv ^ j n ()).coeff n‖ /
    (p ^ (nonsplitWeight d p - 1 / (p - 1))) ^ n

steps.claim: Submultiplicativity: c(n + k) ≤ c(n)·c(k) for all n, k.
steps.lean:
have hc k n : c (n + k) ≤ c n * c k
  have h i := (exists_monomial_max_norm_coeff _ rfl 1 (.single 0 n + .single 1 k)).choose_spec.2 _
    (pow_mem C.translatedWpDeriv_add_mem_multiPhiRing i); simp_all [← subst_pow, ↓Finsupp.prod_pow,
    (· ∘ ·)]
  rw [MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul, sum_eq_single_of_mem (_, _) (by simp; rfl)] at h <;>
    simp [field, Finsupp.ext_iff] at *
  grw [h, H, H k]; ring; repeat tauto
  omega
steps.typed_fact: c (n + k) ≤ c n * c k

steps.claim: φ(x + y)^{j} lies in the two-variable ring 𝔬[[φ(x), φ(y)]] (`translatedWpDeriv_add_mem_multiPhiRing`), so its coefficient at x^n y^k is bounded by the maximal coefficient of that ring at (n, k), attained by a monomial (two-variable version of step 3).
steps.lean:
have h i := (exists_monomial_max_norm_coeff _ rfl 1 (.single 0 n + .single 1 k)).choose_spec.2 _
    (pow_mem C.translatedWpDeriv_add_mem_multiPhiRing i); simp_all [← subst_pow, ↓Finsupp.prod_pow,
    (· ∘ ·)]

steps.claim: The coefficient of x^n y^k of a product of one-variable series in x and y is the product of the coefficients; and the coefficient of x^n y^k of φ(x+y)^j is binom(n+k, n)·(φ^j)_{n+k}.
steps.lean:
rw [MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul, sum_eq_single_of_mem (_, _) (by simp; rfl)] at h <;>
    simp [field, Finsupp.ext_iff] at *

steps.claim: Hence, with the factorials inside the p-adic norms, |(n+k)!·(φ^{j})_{n+k}| ≤ |n!·(φ^{j_n})_n|·|k!·(φ^{j_k})_k| (H at n and k; binom(n+k, n)·n!·k! = (n+k)!); divide by the normalizing powers.
steps.lean: grw [h, H, H k]; ring; repeat tauto

steps.claim: Since c(n) < 1 (the assumption) and c is submultiplicative, the partial sums of c are bounded (∑_{k<K} c(k) ≤ (1 − c(n))⁻¹·∑_{k<n} c(k)), so ∑ c converges and c(k) → 0: there is l with c(k) < |ϖ| for all k ≥ l.
steps.lean:
have ⟨l, hl⟩ := Metric.tendsto_atTop.1 (@summable_of_sum_range_le c _ (by bound) fun _ ↦
    (le_div_iff₀' (by simp_all [field] : 0 < 1 - c n)).2 (by grw [one_sub_mul, sub_le_iff_le_add,
    mul_sum, ← hc, ← sum_range_add, ← le_add_self])).tendsto_atTop_zero ‖ϖ‖ (hϖ ▸ by bound)

steps.claim: Consider the polynomial P = truncation below degree l of S̄ = S mod 𝔪, and the degree of (X − X^{p^e})∘P = P − P^{p^e} (X − X^{p^e} composed after P; `natDegree_comp`: its degree is p^e·deg P).
If (X − X^{p^e})∘P = P − P^{p^e} = X, comparing degrees (q·deg P = 1 is impossible for q = p^e > 1) gives a contradiction; so it suffices to show P − P^{p^e} = X.
It suffices to show it for S̄ itself, i.e. that S̄ equals its truncation P.
S̄ − S̄^{p^e} = X, i.e. (X − X^{p^e})∘S̄ = X: reduce S − S^{p^e} = X + πE modulo 𝔪 (|π| < 1).
S̄ equals its truncation: for k ≥ l the k-th coefficient of S lies in 𝔪; argue by contraposition from c(k) < |ϖ|.
steps.lean: ext k; simp [coeff_trunc]; peel hl k; contrapose this

steps.claim: Take norms of the k-th coefficients in T(ϖX) = ϖS: |ϖ|^k|T_k| = |ϖ|·|S_k|.
steps.lean: apply_fun (‖coeff k ·‖) at hS; simp [*, c, ← rpow_mul_natCast, ← PowerSeries.map.eq_1] at *
grw [← hS, H, ← rpow_le_norm_factorial, mul_div_right_comm, ← rpow_sub] <;> (try ring) <;> bound
